title: structured-output: improve constrained decoding backends for CFG/regex and tokenizer edgecases
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Structured-output constrained decoding is used across function/tool-calling and schema-constrained responses. We've seen corner cases where the regex/CFG backends produce valid constraint matches at the tokenizer level but break streaming or downstream parsers due to token-split boundaries and Unicode edge cases. This PR unifies and hardens the constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) and adds tokenizer-aware fallbacks to prevent broken partial outputs during streaming and compatibility with the OpenAI-style function/schema output flow.

What this changes: - Add tokenizer-aware anchor matching for regex constraints so matches are evaluated on joinable token boundaries rather than raw token ids. This avoids mid-token regex matches that can't be emitted cleanly in streaming. - Improve CFG backend to track nonterminal spans at token granularity and to prefer expansions that resolve before token boundaries used by streaming clients. - Add a tokenizer-unicode fallback: when a regex or CFG anchor fails due to surrogate pair splits or multi-byte grapheme clusters, we attempt a normalized UTF-8 recomposition and retry matching. - Add conservative heuristics for partial streaming emission: we no longer allow emission of a token if it would create a prefix that violates an active constraint unless the runtime has a confirmed fallback route. This reduces broken JSON/object outputs during mid-stream. - Small API compatibility update in openai-compat layer: expose a new optional parameter `tokenizer_safe_mode` for structured output endpoints to opt into the tokenizer-aware matching behavior. Defaults to true for server-side endpoints. - Extensive unit and integration tests for tokenizer edgecases, CFG ambiguity examples, and streaming regression scenarios. - Performance: microbenchmarks show ~1.2% mean latency regression on short responses, negligible for long outputs; batching preserves throughput.

Motivation: Several customer incidents (reproducible with crafted prompts) showed streaming structured outputs emit malformed JSON when regex constraints matched across token splits. This caused downstream parsers and function-call handlers to error, breaking workflows. The fix reduces these incidents by ensuring constraints are respected at the token emission boundary.

Checklist: - [x] Implement tokenizer-aware regex matching - [x] CFG backend token-span tracking - [x] Unicode/grapheme fallback matching - [x] Add openai-compat opt-in param - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration/regression tests added - [x] Benchmarks and perf notes included - [x] Docs note for API parameter
commits_summary:
1) Add tokenizer-aware regex anchor matcher and fallback
2) Refactor CFG decoder to emit token-span metadata
3) Add tokenizer unicode recomposition utility and tests
4) openai-compat: expose tokenizer_safe_mode param and docs
5) Tests: unit + e2e streaming cases and benchmarks
review_comments: Ian Brooks: Can we add a flag to opt out of the tokenizer recomposition in the private runtime? Some customers may want byte-level determinism.
Maya Chen (author): Added `tokenizer_safe_mode` opt-in/out in openai-compat and runtime config; default remains safe.
Sofia Martinez: Regex matcher change looks good but please add a comment about complexity; worst-case regex backtracking could be expensive on long prefixes.
Maya Chen (author): Added a guarded time/length cutoff and unit test for pathological regexes; documented in regex_matcher.rs.
Liam O'Neill: Tests look comprehensive. One nit: prefer smaller helper functions in normalization.rs for readability.
Maya Chen (author): Refactored into two helpers and added comments. Ready for final review.
Sofia Martinez: Approving after CI green.
Ian Brooks: Approved. Leaving merge to release manager.
notes_on_testing: Added 9 new unit tests and 4 integration/e2e tests covering: token-split regex matches, surrogate pair boundaries, grapheme cluster recomposition, CFG ambiguity with streaming. Tests run as part of ci/e2e-structured-output; flaky integration was rerun and passed.
release_notes: structured-output: Harden constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) to be tokenizer-aware and add Unicode/tokenizer fallbacks to prevent malformed streaming structured outputs. Introduces `tokenizer_safe_mode` opt-in parameter to the OpenAI compatibility structured-output endpoint. Minimal perf impact on short responses.
performance_notes: Microbenchmarks show ~1.2% median latency increase on <256 token responses; no measurable throughput loss in batched scenarios. Added benchmarks under benchmarks/constrained_decoding/ for future regression monitoring.
